summary: Speculative but cleanly attributable: the change is gated to bs=8/16/32, and bs=1/128/256 act as untouched in-run controls, so one run reads either way. Fix one build bug first. master's cache1 and cache3 are both views at offset 0 of cache13, so half A's w2 writes would race half B's w13/silu rows. Expect flat to +2%, not 4-8%.
justification: Profile: Marlin is 92.8-94.6% of bs=8/16/32 (105.8/116.0/187.6 us vs floors 37.3/52.5/70.8 us), so it is the only lever there. The per-expert cost is far above the weight-streaming floor: about 20 us/expert at bs=1 and about 15 us/expert at bs=8, against about 5 us/expert of NVFP4 bytes. Marlin is latency- or bytes-in-flight-bound at small M, so more concurrent memory traffic could in principle help. The stated mechanism (ramp/tail plus inter-kernel gaps) is mostly the wrong one. Shape time minus kernel sum at bs=32 is only about 3 us (200.7 vs about 197.5), so hiding the silu launch and graph gaps is worth at most about 1.5%. Marlin's stripe partitioning also spreads every m-block across all SMs, so there is little per-expert tail to fill. The gain can only come from the two Marlin kernels' CTAs being co-resident on the same SMs. Weakest link: Marlin launches one CTA per SM and, as far as I recall, requests the device's max dynamic smem (in vLLM's marlin, launched with max_shared_mem). If so, the side stream's CTAs land only as the first kernel's retire, and the overlap collapses to the two kernel boundaries. The cost is certain: two extra Marlin launches (about 2-4 us each per the marlin-two-class review), an extra silu, a fork/join and a 2-CTA align, about 5-8 us. LESSONS also lists several flat or losing side-stream attempts (moe-align-side-stream, fa3-scheduler-metadata-side-stream). Two more weak points. (1) A fixed split by local id 0-15/16-31 under skewed popularity can leave one half with most of the routes, which shrinks any concurrency gain at bs=8 (about 7 experts). (2) Each half now spreads half the work over the same persistent grid, so fixed per-kernel cost (prologue, k-stripe lock reduction) doubles. The expected directions are consistent with the gating: bs=1/128/256 flat (code paths byte-identical), bs=8 the smallest effect. The 4-8% at bs=32 is optimistic; I expect flat to +2% at bs=32 and flat-to-slower at bs=8.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity: supplies the cache13 buffer with cache1 = cache13[:n*8*2I] and cache3 = cache13[:n*8*H], both at offset 0. This is safe serially but a cross-stream data race here: cache3 row r overlaps cache1 row r//2, which may belong to the other half and be unread by its silu. Allocate cache3 (or the y buffer) separately. Otherwise a correctness failure, or a silently different result, comes from the interaction, not the idea.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: the halves kernel is a re-parameterisation of its _align_small_kernel and keeps SGLang's block_size_m pick at bs<=32 (8 / 16). Any change in align cost (2-CTA grid, two stacked outputs) lands in the same 2.7-4.4 us row and is part of this hypothesis's measured cost, not a separate effect. Read the align row separately.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: runs after the join on the full local_ids, which program 0 must write in full (remote routes as -1, both halves' routes as local ids). If program 0 writes only its half, the post-norm silently drops half B. Not a performance confounder.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: touches only num_tokens >= 128, which this change leaves untouched. No confounding; its bs=128/256 rows are the in-run flat control.
interference: No companion warranted. The change is single-area and shape-gated, and bs=1/128/256 run master's code byte-for-byte in the same run, so a per-shape move at bs=8/16/32 beyond the paired-ratio noise is attributable to the two-stream split. A gain is unambiguous: splitting the halves serially on one stream can only add launches, so any net gain must come from overlap. A loss is mildly ambiguous between 'no overlap' and 'overlap smaller than the 5-8 us overhead'. A serialized-halves control (the same split on one stream) would separate the two, but it cannot change the decision: either way the follow-up is to drop the idea or to gate it to bs=32. With 2 moe checks left it is not worth a check. Noise: DECISIONS records unchanged bs=32 rows spanning 147-265 us across runs, so read only the paired ratio against SGLang within the run and the bs=8/16/32 rows, never the absolute Marlin row sum. The four Marlin rows will sum higher by construction, as the hypothesis notes.
rules_flags: No rule problem in the design: branching on num_tokens is allowed, the side stream, second workspace and halves-kernel compile live in prepare(), nothing derived from data is cached, and there are no host syncs. Use torch.cuda.current_stream() at call time; do not cache the capture stream in prepare.
Correctness (not a rule but run-fatal): cache1/cache3 aliasing across streams as above. Give cache3 its own allocation (or size cache13 as n*8*(2I+H) with disjoint offsets) before the fork.

None of the 5 pre-timing tests (bs 4, 33, 257, 128-skewed, 1) exercises the 8..32 halves path, so the first real check of the two-stream pipeline is the timed calls themselves. A race would show up there, possibly intermittently. In prepare(), add an untimed, synthetic-input end-to-end self-check: the halves pipeline vs master's single-stream pipeline at bs=8/16/32, bitwise or rel-L2 1e-3, with a print and a fallback to master's path on mismatch. The extended align self-check alone does not cover the GEMM/silu/cache sharing.

Make every buffer that half B touches (cache1/cache2/cache3, sorted_ids_h, block_experts_h, local_ids_h, topk_weights) exist before side.wait_stream(current). Join with current.wait_stream(side) before the post-norm and before returning. Any c_tmp or other allocation Marlin's wrapper makes inside the side-stream context is fine under graph capture.
open_questions: Does SGLang's moe_wna16_marlin_gemm launch with the device's max dynamic smem (one CTA per SM)? If so, two concurrent Marlin kernels cannot co-reside and the expected gain is about the kernel boundaries only. The profile's per-kernel durations will show it: if each half's Marlin row is about half of master's and they do not overlap in time, there was no concurrency.

Split balance: under skewed routing a fixed 0-15/16-31 split can be lopsided. A follow-up could have the align kernel pick the halves on device: a greedy by-count assignment computed from the one-hot counts, which needs no host branch and so is legal. This is only worth trying if this run shows any overlap gain.
If bs=32 gains and bs=8 loses, the hypothesis already plans an ab-tune gating to bs >= 16. Gating to bs=32 alone may be the right cut, since bs=16 has only about 12 experts.

risk: high means this cannot be a scored run, and moe has 2 checks left today. Spend one check on it only if nothing better is queued (swapab-w13-silu-epilogue-verify is queued and unheld; compare priorities).
